sections.html:
The capital of New Mexico also serves as the seat of Santa Fe County. It rests against the Sangre de Cristo foothills at 6,998 feet, higher than any other state capital, and held 87,505 people at the 2020 census across about 52.4 square miles. Spanish colonists founded it in 1610, making it the nation's oldest state capital, and its Pueblo Revival and Territorial Revival adobe buildings are largely preserved. A seller may therefore own a house governed by rules unknown in other cities.

State and local government supply roughly 15,000 jobs, the most of any sector, with education and health services and then leisure and hospitality behind it. Over 250 galleries make tourism and the arts central. Jobs tied to budgets and visitors mean demand can swing with the season, so ask any buyer how long they need to close.

A typical year brings 12.79 inches of precipitation and 20.2 inches of snow. The 24-hour average temperature climbs from 30.3 degrees in December to 70.1 in July, which makes heating a real expense for much of the year.

Wildfire is a local worry. The Santa Fe Fire Department has ten full-time employees who specialize in fuel management where homes meet wildland, and it offers free Wildfire Home Hazard Assessments and evacuation zone information. If your house backs onto open land, an assessment report shows a buyer what you have done.

  • Ask the fire department for a home hazard assessment before listing.
  • Keep records of brush clearing or roof work.
  • Review your homeowner insurance terms, since buyers ask about them.

Five historic districts cover parts of the city. A review board examines alterations that staff cannot approve, designates historic status, approves new construction and weighs changes to existing buildings, meeting on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month. A buyer who wants to change a front facade, windows or walls inside a district may need review first.

If your house sits in a district, tell any buyer early, and ask the Historic Preservation Division what is on file for the address. Questions go to historicpreservation@santafenm.gov and submittals to hpdsubmittal@santafenm.gov, so you can ask in writing what has been approved or filed.

Every short-term rental in Santa Fe needs a business registration plus either a Residential Short-Term Rental Permit or a Non-Residential Short-Term Rental Registration, depending on zoning. Anyone planning to own or run a short-term rental in calendar year 2026 must obtain a permit, and within 10 days of issuance or renewal the owner must notify required parties by first-class mail.

If your house has run as a rental, give the buyer its permit status in writing. A new owner cannot assume the permit is theirs without checking the city's rules.

sections.h2: Santa Fe County property tax dates
sections.html:
Valuation belongs to the County Assessor and collection to the County Treasurer, whose office mails about 60,000 real property, personal property and mobile home bills yearly.

Tax stepDetail
Notice of ValueMailed in spring, with 30 days from mailing to appeal or apply for exemptions
Bills mailedOn or before November 1
First halfDue November 10, delinquent after December 10
Second halfDue on or before May 10
Interest1% a month after 30 days
Penalty1% a month, capped at 5%, with a $5 minimum
Assessor phone505-986-6300
Treasurer office100 Catron St, Santa Fe

If you are selling a house that carried a special exemption, ask the Assessor how that exemption transfers to a new owner. The Treasurer's payment platforms charge a card fee of 2.5% and a flat $1.95 e-check fee, so ask how a payment at closing will be made before you assume a method.

Owing tax does not prevent a sale. The balance comes out of your proceeds at closing together with any mortgage or lien. Phone the Treasurer before you say yes to an offer, and have the title company recheck near the signing date, since interest and penalty accrue monthly.

sections.h2: Getting around: roads, rail and schools
sections.html: Santa Fe Public Schools serves the city. Interstate 25, U.S. 84, U.S. 285 and NM 599 run through the area, the Rail Runner Express stops at four Santa Fe stations, and Santa Fe Regional Airport handles local flights. Los Alamos National Laboratory is about a 45-minute drive away.

Adobe walls behave differently from frame construction. Buyers and inspectors look at roof drainage, cracked stucco, moisture at the base of walls and the age of heating equipment, because winters are cold. If the house sits in a historic district, they also want to know whether past changes were reviewed. A cash buyer accepts these questions as part of the deal and prices the house accordingly, while a financed buyer may ask for repairs before closing.

Before listing, walk the exterior and write down what you find. A page of dated notes on the roof, stucco and any past review board approvals gives buyers confidence and speeds up their offers.

Many Santa Fe houses are second homes that stand empty for months. An empty house needs a plan for winter: heat set high enough to protect pipes, someone to check on it, and a clear record of who holds the keys. If you live elsewhere, choose a local contact for the walkthrough and ask the title company how to sign documents from a distance. Selling an unoccupied house to a cash buyer can avoid repeated trips for showings and repairs.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you talk to buyers
sections.html: Collect the latest tax bill and note what is paid. Gather paperwork for any review board approval, rental permit or wildfire assessment. List known repairs on the roof, heating and walls. Decide whether time or price matters more, then compare a listing against a cash offer by what you would actually net. Finally, pick a title company early and ask it what documents it needs, so nothing slows the closing.

sections.h2: Your options for selling in Santa Fe
sections.html:
A seller can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer.

  • List with an agent: wide exposure, though it may involve inspections, repair requests and staging for a Santa Fe buyer.
  • Sell on your own: saves a commission but leaves paperwork and negotiation to you.
  • Cash offer: from a buyer who buys the house as it stands. Ask for it in writing and read it closely.

Cash sales often fit owners who inherited a house, hold a vacant second home, or face repairs on an older adobe. Whichever route you pick, gather the tax bill, any review board paperwork, rental permits and repair records before you talk to a buyer.

faqs.q: What county is Santa Fe in?
faqs.a: Santa Fe County. The city is both the county seat and the state capital.

faqs.q: When are Santa Fe County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Mailing is on or before November 1. Pay the first half by November 10, since it is delinquent after December 10, and the second half on or before May 10.

faqs.q: How many historic districts does Santa Fe have?
faqs.a: Five. The Historic Districts Review Board reviews work that staff cannot approve administratively.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to run a short-term rental in Santa Fe?
faqs.a: Yes. Every short-term rental needs a business registration and a permit or registration, depending on zoning, and an owner who plans to operate in 2026 must obtain a permit.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Santa Fe house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers take it as-is, and a listing can close without repairs when the buyer agrees. Weigh your net on each.
